title: District of Columbia Cash Bail Reform Act of 2025
official_title: To require mandatory pretrial and post conviction detention for crimes of violence and dangerous crimes and require mandatory cash bail for certain offenses that pose a threat to public safety or order in the District of Columbia, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Stefanik (R-NY) with 3 cosponsors; passed the Republican-majority House. Federal changes to the District of Columbia's bail and detention laws would need 60 votes in the Senate and are likely to draw strong Democratic opposition over federal intervention in D.C., making passage unlikely.
summary: Requires judges in the District of Columbia to detain people charged with violent or dangerous crimes before trial, and to require cash bail for certain public-safety offenses.
brief: Mandates pretrial detention for violent and dangerous crimes and cash bail for certain offenses in the District of Columbia.

top_lines.headline: Mandatory Detention
subs: Judges must detain those charged with violent or dangerous crimes before trial
Same mandatory detention applies after conviction
Expands the 'dangerous crime' and 'crime of violence' definitions

top_lines.headline: Mandatory Cash Bail
subs: Secured cash bail required for 'public safety or order' crimes
Covers offenses such as rioting, stalking, and fleeing police

items.main: Names the Act the “District of Columbia Cash Bail Reform Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Mandatory Pretrial and Post Conviction Detention for Crime of Violence or Dangerous Crime

items.main: Requires D.C. judges to detain people charged with a crime of violence or dangerous crime before trial, and after conviction.
items.detail: Amends the D.C. Official Code so a judicial officer must order pretrial detention for anyone charged with a crime of violence or dangerous crime, and applies mandatory detention after conviction for the same. The definitions of 'dangerous crime' and 'crime of violence' are expanded to include first-degree burglary and robbery, attempts, and those committed with a dangerous weapon.

sections.label: Section 3 — Requiring Cash Bail for Release of Individuals Charged With Public Safety or Order Offenses

items.main: Requires a secured cash bail bond for release of people charged with 'public safety or order' crimes.
items.detail: Adds a category of 'public safety or order crime' — including failure to appear, obstruction of justice, fleeing law enforcement, rioting, inciting a riot, destruction of property, stalking, and certain burglary or robbery — for which a person may be released only on a secured appearance bond (cash or surety). It defines 'secured appearance bond' and adds surety-arrest provisions. The changes apply to offenses charged 30 days after enactment.

items.main: Applies the Act and its amendments to individuals charged with an offense in D.C. on or after 30 days after enactment.
items.detail: Effective-date/applicability provision — sets when the changes take effect; no independent substantive effect.

criticisms.why: Mr. Speaker, I strongly oppose this bill which amends the District of Columbia's pretrial release and detention law. Last year, violent crime in D.C. was down 35 percent, reaching an over-30-year low. This year, violent crime in D.C. is down 28 percent compared to the same period last year.

gaps: The bill mandates detention and cash bail but does not provide funding for additional D.C. jail capacity.
It requires secured bonds for certain offenses but does not address defendants who cannot afford to post bail.

Last year, violent crime in D.C. was down 35 percent, reaching an over-30-year low. This year, violent crime in D.C. is down 28 percent compared to the same period last year.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Walkinshaw
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, 2 months ago, I was a local government official not far from here, in Fairfax County. In the 6 years I spent in that role, I learned that the people best positioned to make decisions about the local policies in their local communities are local leaders after listening to that local community. My colleagues across the aisle who are advocating for these bills, with due respect, know very little about the District of Columbia, know very little outside of perhaps their walk from their apartment in Navy Yard to this Capitol complex.

added: Mandatory cash bail (secured appearance bond) for D.C. 'public safety or order' crimes
modified: D.C. Official Code requires pretrial and post-conviction detention for crimes of violence and dangerous crimes; the definitions of those crimes are expanded
"Public safety or order crime" definition narrows robbery the same way as burglary — excluding first-degree or dangerous-weapon robbery, instead of treating all robbery as a qualifying offense
